title: Creaking when turning the wheel
h1: Why does my car creak or groan when I turn the steering wheel?
metaDesc: Creaking or groaning when you turn the steering wheel? Answer a few questions to see if it's a strut mount, ball joint or bushing, how urgent it is, and what to do.
synonyms: creaking noise when turning steering wheel
creak when turning at low speed
creaking noise when turning and going over bumps
creaking in cold weather when turning
intro: A creak or groan when you turn the wheel usually comes from a rubber or metal joint in the steering or front suspension that's dry or worn. Often it's a minor wear item, but some of those joints hold the wheel to the car, so it's worth finding out which one it is. These questions help you tell which is which.
safety: If the steering suddenly feels loose, the car wanders, or a front wheel looks tilted, pull over and don't drive it.
If you hear a loud bang or clunk and the steering changes, stop as soon as it's safe and call for a tow.
If the steering suddenly gets very hard to turn, slow down and pull over carefully.

q_feel.q: Besides the noise, how does the steering feel?
q_feel.help: "Loose" means the wheel moves a bit before the car responds, or you're constantly correcting to stay straight.

opts.a: Loose or vague, the car wanders, the wheel is crooked, or there's a heavy clunk
Heavier than usual, or there's a whine as well as the groan
It feels normal. It's just the noise

q_when.q: When do you hear the creak most?

opts.a: Turning the wheel at low speed or while parking
Turning while going over bumps, dips or driveways
Mostly in cold or wet weather, and it fades as the car warms up
Only in very tight turns, with a scrubbing or hopping feeling

q_source.q: Where does the sound seem to come from?
q_source.help: Try turning the wheel back and forth with the car stopped and the engine running, with a window down.

opts.a: Up near the top of a front wheel, sometimes with a pop or a small jolt in the steering wheel
Low down near a front wheel, a dry creak like an old door hinge
Inside the car: the steering column, the dash or the wheel itself

result.title: A worn steering or suspension joint may be close to failing
result.now: Don't drive it. Have the car towed or have a mobile mechanic inspect the front end.
if: If you're on the road when it starts, slow down gently, avoid hard braking and sharp turns, and pull over as soon as it's safe.
If a front wheel leans in or out at the top, a ball joint may have separated. Don't move the car at all.
result.why: Creaking plus loose steering or a heavy clunk suggests a ball joint or tie rod end is badly worn. These parts connect the wheels to the car and the steering. If one separates, you can lose control of that wheel.

causes.name: Badly worn ball joint
causes.clues: Creaking and clunking over bumps, uneven tire wear, a wheel that looks tilted.

causes.name: Worn tie rod end
causes.clues: Play in the steering wheel and wandering at highway speed.

causes.name: Broken coil spring or control arm mount
causes.clues: One corner sits lower than the others, or a loud clunk when turning.

you: Without moving the car, look at the front wheels from the front. Note if one leans in or out at the top, and tell the shop or tow driver.
shop: Ball joint and tie rod inspection with the wheels off the ground
Front suspension inspection on a lift

result.title: The power steering may not be giving full assist
result.now: If your car has a power steering fluid reservoir, check the level with the engine off. Get the steering checked within the next few days, and avoid highway driving and long trips until then.
if: If the steering becomes very hard to turn, or a steering warning light comes on, don't drive it. Have it towed.
If the fluid is low, top it up with the type in your owner's manual and have the leak found. If it's dripping steadily, don't drive it until it's checked.
If the steering gets heavier while you're driving, or the fluid level keeps dropping, stop driving it and have it checked before going further.
If you smell hot fluid or see smoke from under the hood, pull over, turn the engine off and step away. Power steering fluid on hot parts can burn.
result.why: A groan with heavier steering often means the power steering isn't giving full assist. On cars with hydraulic steering, low fluid or a worn pump are common causes, and a shop will usually find the leak or pressure-test the pump before replacing anything. On electric steering, it can be a motor or sensor fault.

causes.name: Low power steering fluid from a leak
causes.clues: A low reservoir, or reddish or amber drips under the front.
causes.against: Doesn't apply if your car has electric power steering with no reservoir.

causes.name: Worn power steering pump
causes.clues: The fluid level is fine but the groan or whine is getting louder.

causes.name: Electric power steering fault
causes.clues: A steering warning light, or the heaviness comes and goes.

you: Check the power steering fluid level, if your car has a reservoir.
Look under the front of the car for fresh drips.
shop: Power steering fluid and leak inspection
Code scan for electric steering faults

result.title: Possibly a dry or worn ball joint
result.now: Have the front suspension inspected within the next few days. Until then, avoid potholes, curbs and sharp turns at speed.
if: If the steering starts feeling loose, the car wanders, or you hear clunking, stop driving it and have it towed.
If a shop finds the joint is only dry and not loose, it may just need grease, if it's the type that can be greased.
If a front wheel looks tilted in or out at the top, don't move the car. Have it towed.
If you hear a loud bang or clunk and the steering changes, stop as soon as it's safe and call for a tow.
result.why: Ball joints are pivots that let the front wheels steer and move up and down. When the grease inside dries out or the joint wears, it creaks as it moves, especially when you turn and hit a bump at the same time. A worn ball joint gets worse over time and can eventually separate, so a shop will usually check it for play with the wheels off the ground to tell a dry joint from a worn one.

causes.name: Worn or dry lower ball joint
causes.clues: A creak like a squeaky door when turning over bumps, coming from low near the wheel.

causes.name: Torn ball joint boot
causes.clues: A split rubber boot lets grease out and dirt in.

causes.name: Worn control arm bushing
causes.clues: Creaking over bumps even when driving straight.

you: Bounce the front of the car by pushing down on it while parked and listen for the creak.
Look behind the front wheels for torn rubber boots.
shop: Ball joint play check with the wheels off the ground
Front suspension inspection on a lift

result.title: Possibly dry rubber bushings, often in the sway bar or control arms
result.now: Book a front suspension check when convenient, and mention that it's worse in cold or wet weather.
if: If the creak becomes a clunk, or it starts happening in warm weather too, get it checked within a few days.
If the steering feels loose or the car wanders, stop driving it and have it checked right away.
If you hear a loud bang or clunk and the steering changes, stop as soon as it's safe and call for a tow.
result.why: The suspension uses rubber bushings to cushion metal parts. As they age, they harden and creak when they twist, and cold or wet weather makes it worse. Dry bushings are often more noise than danger, but only an inspection can rule out a worn joint, and worn bushings can affect handling and tire wear over time.

causes.name: Dry or worn sway bar bushings
causes.clues: Creaking over bumps and in turns, worse in the cold.

causes.name: Worn control arm bushings
causes.clues: Creaking plus a slight clunk when braking or accelerating.

causes.name: Dry strut mount
causes.clues: The creak is near the top of the wheel when turning.

you: Note whether the noise happens only when the weather is cold or damp.
Bounce the front of the car while parked and listen.
shop: Sway bar link and bushing check

result.title: Possibly the tires scrubbing in tight turns, which can be normal
result.now: Check your tire pressures and set them to the numbers on the sticker inside the driver's door. If you have 4WD or AWD with a selectable mode, make sure it's in 2WD or Auto on dry pavement.
if: If you have a part-time 4WD system that's engaged on dry pavement, switch it off. Driving that way can damage the drivetrain.
If the noise or hopping happens in normal turns too, or the 4WD warning light is on, book a check.
If the steering feels loose, the car wanders, or you hear clunking, stop driving it and have it checked right away.
result.why: At full lock, the front tires turn at slightly different angles and can scrub on the pavement, which makes a groan, especially on smooth parking garage floors. A 4WD system locked in on dry pavement causes a similar binding or hopping feel. If the noise happens outside those tight turns, it's worth an inspection rather than assuming it's normal.

causes.name: Normal tire scrub at full lock
causes.clues: Only in very tight turns on smooth floors, and nothing else is wrong.

causes.name: 4WD engaged on dry pavement
causes.clues: A part-time 4WD truck or SUV with 4WD switched on.

causes.name: AWD or differential problem
causes.clues: Binding or shuddering in turns even in normal mode, or mismatched tires.

you: Check that all four tires are inflated correctly.
Check the 4WD selector or dash indicator.
Make sure all four tires are the same size and similarly worn.

result.title: Possibly a worn strut mount or strut bearing
result.now: Book a front suspension check when convenient. Mention that the creak or pop happens when turning at low speed.
if: If you feel a jolt or clunk through the wheel over bumps, or the steering feels notchy, get it checked within a few days.
If the steering starts feeling loose or the car wanders, stop driving it and have it checked right away.
If one front corner suddenly sits lower or you heard a loud bang, a coil spring may have broken. Don't drive it until it's checked.
result.why: On many cars, the top of each front strut sits in a mount with a bearing that rotates when you steer. When the bearing wears or the rubber dries out, it creaks, groans or pops as you turn, especially at low speed. It's often not urgent, but it tends to get worse, and a technician should confirm the noise isn't from a ball joint or spring.

causes.name: Worn strut bearing
causes.clues: A creak or pop when turning while parked, sometimes felt in the steering wheel.

causes.name: Worn strut mount rubber
causes.clues: A clunk over bumps along with the creak.

causes.name: Worn strut or broken coil spring
causes.clues: One corner sits lower or the car bounces more than usual.

you: With a window down, turn the wheel back and forth while parked and note which side the sound comes from.
Check whether one front corner sits lower than the other.
shop: Front suspension inspection on a lift

result.title: The noise may be in the steering column or trim, not the suspension
result.now: With the car parked, turn the wheel slowly and see whether the steering wheel cover or the plastic trim around the column is rubbing.
if: If the airbag warning light is on, have the car checked soon. A worn clock spring inside the steering wheel can affect the airbag and horn.
If the steering feels notchy, sticks, catches, or has play before the wheels respond, don't drive it until it's checked. A worn steering shaft joint affects your control of the car.
result.why: If the creak comes from inside the car, the cause is usually something rubbing in the steering column or the trim around it. Trim rubbing is a comfort issue, but a worn steering shaft joint or clock spring can sound similar, so it's worth having a technician confirm which it is.

causes.name: Steering wheel or column trim rubbing
causes.clues: The creak changes when you press on the plastic around the column.

causes.name: Dry or worn steering shaft joint
causes.clues: A creak or slight clunk felt through the wheel, often heard by the driver's feet.

causes.name: Worn clock spring
causes.clues: A rubbing sound inside the wheel, sometimes with the airbag light or horn not working.

you: Press gently on the column trim while turning the wheel and listen for changes.
Check whether the airbag light is off after the car starts.
shop: Airbag system code scan if the light is on

result.title: Have the steering and front suspension inspected
result.now: Book a front-end inspection when convenient. Record a short video with sound of the creak while turning the wheel to show the technician.
if: If the steering feels loose, the car wanders, or you hear clunking, stop driving it and have it checked right away.
If the steering gets heavier or you hear a whine, check the power steering fluid, if your car has a reservoir.
If a front wheel looks tilted, or the steering suddenly gets very hard to turn, pull over and don't drive it.
result.why: Creaks when turning come from a handful of joints in the steering and suspension. A technician can check them all for wear in a few minutes with the car on a lift.

causes.name: Worn strut mount or bearing
causes.clues: Creaking or popping at low speed when turning.

causes.name: Dry or worn ball joint
causes.clues: Creaking when turning over bumps.

causes.name: Dry suspension bushings
causes.clues: Worse in cold or wet weather.

you: Note whether it happens parked, at low speed, over bumps, or only in cold weather.
Bounce the front of the car while parked and listen.
shop: Front suspension inspection on a lift
Ball joint and tie rod check
